title: Competitors and market
purpose: When a rival moves on price, offer, product or ads, or I need to know where we can win, open Competitors to see what changed, whether it touches our sales, and what to do about it.
fires: Checking rival sites and Instagram by hand, the spy tool subscription nobody reads, the agency's once-a-year competitor deck, and the gut sense that a rival is stealing buyers.
not_for: A brand that is the only seller of what it makes, or one that sells mostly wholesale where the retailer sets the rivals; and anyone who wants rival ads to copy.

jobs.job: When a rival cuts price or starts a sale that could take my buyers this week, tell me the same day and how much of our sales it touches, so I decide to match, hold or answer with value
jobs.circumstance: Tuesday, our daily sales dipped 15 percent, and a rival quietly went 30 percent off our matched best seller yesterday

progress.functional: know which rival moved, on which products, by how much, and our sales on those products
progress.emotional: stop the paranoia of checking rival sites every day
progress.social: give the team a clear response plan instead of a panic

jobs.hire_today: checking rival sites and emails by hand, a price tool that alerts on everything, or finding out from a sales dip
jobs.fire: the hand checks and the noisy price alerts

forces.push: every day of not knowing loses sales or leads to a panic discount
forces.pull: the move, the products it touches and the dollars at stake
forces.habit: I sign up to their emails and see what lands
forces.anxiety: what if I match a price I did not need to match

jobs.little_hire: any day a rival moves, checked daily

watch.metric: our price against tracked rivals on matched products, and our sales on those products, daily

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a rival sale was seen 5 days late, after a 20 percent dip. After: it is seen the same day and answered with a bundle, and the dip is held to 5 percent.
jobs.not_for: a brand whose products have no close match at any rival

jobs.job: When costs rise and rivals start raising prices, tell me who raised, by how much, and whether we have room to raise too, so we protect margin without being the first to move alone
jobs.circumstance: Our landed cost is up 10 percent, and 3 rivals raised prices last month

progress.functional: know rival price moves over 90 days on matched products, and our gap to the range
progress.emotional: stop the fear of being the only one to raise

jobs.hire_today: checking rival sites, or gut feel

forces.push: holding price while costs rise eats margin
forces.pull: rival rises shown with our gap
forces.anxiety: what if we lose buyers who were comparing

jobs.little_hire: each quarter, and when our costs rise

watch.metric: rival price changes on matched products, 90 day, and our gap to the middle of the range

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: we held price while 3 rivals rose 8 percent. After: we raise 6 percent with no drop in conversion.
jobs.not_for: a brand whose costs are flat and whose price already sits at the top of the range

jobs.job: When I set or review prices, check that ours sit inside the range buyers expect for this category next to rivals, so we are not priced out or leaving money on the table
jobs.circumstance: A price review, rivals from $12 to $28 a pair, we are at $17, and I am not sure where the buyer's line is

progress.functional: know our price per unit against the rival range, same pack size
progress.social: defend the price to the team and to retailers

jobs.hire_today: a spreadsheet of rival prices made once, or gut feel

forces.push: the wrong price costs volume or margin on every order
forces.pull: a current price ladder with ours marked
forces.habit: price near the rival I know best
forces.anxiety: what if pack sizes and quality make the match unfair

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before any price change

watch.metric: our price per unit against the tracked rival range, same pack size, monthly
watch.source: rival price capture, our price list

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: priced 8 percent under the middle of the range, with a premium story. After: raised 10 percent, conversion flat and margin up 4 points.
jobs.not_for: a one-of-a-kind product with no rival at a matched pack size

jobs.job: When I catch myself scrolling rival Instagram and sites at night, tell me which rival moves matter to our sales and let me ignore the rest, so I can stop watching them
jobs.circumstance: 11 pm, phone in hand, checking what a rival posted today

progress.functional: see only the rival moves that touch our sales or price
progress.emotional: be free of the rival obsession

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. The scrolling is the workaround

forces.push: hours lost and anxiety every week
forces.pull: a short weekly note with only what matters
forces.anxiety: what if I miss the one move that mattered

jobs.little_hire: weekly, with same-day alerts only for big moves

watch.metric: rival alerts per week that led to an action

drives.metric: owner hours on planned work per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 hours a week on rival checks. After: 20 minutes, with 1 real move acted on each month.
jobs.not_for: an owner who does not watch rivals at all and sleeps fine

jobs.job: When we keep running sales to keep up, tell me whether we discount deeper or more often than rivals while claiming to be premium, so we stop training buyers to wait

jobs.not_for: a brand with no investors or board asking

jobs.job: When a rival wins buyers with a claim that looks false, like a fake "was" price or an unproven health claim, show me the evidence and my options, so I decide whether to act without starting a fight I lose
jobs.circumstance: A rival says "clinically proven" with no study behind it, and their ads beat ours

progress.functional: know the claim, the proof it lacks and the ways to report it
progress.emotional: stop stewing about an unfair rival

jobs.hire_today: a lawyer, or nothing

forces.push: false claims win buyers from honest brands
forces.pull: evidence gathered and options named
forces.anxiety: what if acting starts a legal fight

watch.metric: rival claims flagged with evidence, and outcomes of reports

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a false claim ran for 9 months. After: it is reported with evidence and removed in 6 weeks.
jobs.not_for: a category with no claims that need proof
